youtube_title: Kingsford Heights, Indiana: the empty wartime town and the plant next door
youtube:
You asked for Kingsford Heights! In 1942, the government built a whole town in LaPorte County for workers at the Kingsbury Ordnance Plant next door. It was first called Victory City. Thousands of homes went up, but many workers kept their own homes, and most of the new houses stood empty. A 1944 newspaper headline called it a "New Deal Ghost Town." Hundreds of houses were shipped off to cities like Evansville and Green Bay, and the families who stayed bought the land from the government and incorporated the town. But the plant next door left something in the ground: Defense Department cleanup data from 2015 listed lead, arsenic, mercury and TNT in soil and groundwater at sites on the old plant grounds, outside town. Part of that land is now the Kingsbury Fish & Wildlife Area, and its map marks some spots "Contaminated Area/No Trespassing." Comment your town, and it could be next! #KingsfordHeights #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #WW2 #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Town of Kingsford Heights (townofkingsfordheights.com); Jeff Kenney, "Victory City," Towne Post (2022); The History Museum, South Bend; "New Deal Ghost Town," Garfield County News (Panguitch, Utah), Sept. 28, 1944, via Utah Digital Newspapers; Indiana Public Media, A Moment of Indiana History; Clio, "Diamond Villa Housing" (Evansville); Wisconsin Historical Society, property record HI245038 (Green Bay); ProPublica, "Bombs in Your Backyard" (2017; Defense Department cleanup data, 2015); U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Formerly Used Defense Sites program; Indiana DNR, Kingsbury Fish & Wildlife Area maps (2022, 2025). More LaPorte County history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

note: Viewer request passed along by Scoop, Nov. 16, 2026 ('we have requests for fish lake and kingsford heights'). Eerie history, not a legend: none found for the town. Remade Nov. 16, 2026 at Scoop's request ('remake kingsbury and kingsford heights to include how toxic and contaminated from the munitions plant it is'): the ghost-town story is kept, shortened, and the plant's contamination added (the Defense Department's 2015 cleanup data for the old plant grounds, outside town, and the DNR map's 'Contaminated Area/No Trespassing'). The first version (commit f66d744) never aired. Nov. 16, 8 PM: re-voiced so 'lead' (the metal) is said 'led' (story 'say' rule \b([Ll])ead\b -> \1ed, voice only; captions unchanged); 52.6 s, check all good, true peak -2.4 dBFS.
factcheck: Blind independent check Nov. 16, 2026 (script, on-screen text and pictures only), then a second check of the changes: 'Nearly 3,000 houses went up' became 'Thousands of homes went up' (3,000 planned; 2,974 in the 1944 story; 'more than 2,600 dormitories, trailers, and prefabricated homes' per IMH); the headline card names the Garfield County News, Sept. 28, 1944 (Utah Digital Newspapers record), without '(UTAH)', which isn't printed on the scan; 'bought the town' became 'bought the land from the government and incorporated the town'; the unverifiable aerial ring plan was dropped and 'curved in rings around a town center' became 'laid out in long curves, not a grid'; first label '1940s'. Second check: all supported. Remake: three blind checks Nov. 16 (each on script, text and pictures only). Fixes: 'list' became 'data from 2015 listed' (ProPublica 2017, from DoD data last updated in 2015); 'at sites on the old plant grounds, outside town' (the Army Corps' mapped sites are miles from the town center, with no overlap with the town boundary); 'packed up' dropped; the plume drawings stay put and nothing is built over them, the first one under the plant's fenced grounds; the end card shows the wildlife area, not the town's houses; credits drop Wikipedia and the unchecked DHPA survey. Third check: all supported.
